objectives.text: act out the conversation that begins “How was your weekend?” about an amusement park
tell how their weekend was with words like great, exciting and boring
name weekend activities: see a musical, sail on a boat, build a model plane, have a sleepover
ask and answer “What did she do on the weekend?” using past words like ate and saw
read “My First Bike Ride” from the Netherlands and retell the writer's story in order
act out the trip planning conversation that begins “I've just finished making the hotel reservation.”
name vacation activities: go snorkeling, go whale watching, explore a cave, ride a camel
say what will probably happen: “He'll probably go rafting.” “She probably won't go on a cruise.”
ask and answer “What will he do during vacation?” about their own vacation plans
read “A Vacation in Iceland” and tell what visitors can see and do there
learn how a play, an opera and a musical are alike and different
write a report about a play, opera or musical showing in their city
join two short sentences into one with and, but or so
tell the class why they would or would not like to see the show
act out the conversation that begins “Excuse me. I'm looking for a bank.”
give directions with go down this street, turn right and walk one block
use movement words: into, out of, up, down, over, under, around, through
describe movement, like “He came down the stairs and walked out of the house.”
read “Going for a Walk” from Germany and find the words that tell where things move
act out the robotics club conversation that begins “Welcome to our robotics club!”
name school clubs and what members do: drama club, science club, build model rockets, draw comics
ask and answer “What's she interested in?” with “She's interested in acting in school plays.”
guess which club someone will join, like “She'll probably join the drama club.”
read “Robotic Fun” from the UK and tell what they learned about building robots
learn road safety rules for crossing the street and riding a bike
write a report about traffic signs and what each one means
fix run-on sentences by splitting them or joining them with and, but or so
explain to a partner why one traffic sign is important for safety
act out the conversation that begins “Your uncle is coming to visit this weekend.”
name places in town: library, post office, police station, train station, art museum
match places with what people do there: borrow books, mail a package, wait for the train
ask and answer “What was he doing there?” with “He was waiting for the train.”
read “Oriental Pearl TV Tower” about China and tell facts about the tower
act out the school parade conversation that begins “Our class is going to march in the school parade.”
tell what they would dress up as for a parade, like Peter Pan
name fair activities: ride a unicycle, pose for pictures, take a selfie, make masks
ask and answer “What were they doing at the fair when it started to snow?”
read “Chanthaburi Fruit Festival” from Thailand and tell what people do at the festival
learn about rain, snow, sleet and hail and how they fall from clouds
make a bar graph of the average precipitation each month in a city
use their graph to tell which month gets the most and least rain or snow
write the names of people with capital letters, like Ted and Mary
act out the muffin conversation that begins “Mom, can we make muffins?”
name amounts: a bottle of ketchup, a box of cereal, a bunch of grapes, a carton of eggs
tell what someone bought, like “She bought two cartons of milk and a bottle of ketchup.”
make a shopping list for muffins and say how much of each thing they need
read “Flea Markets” about Finland and tell what people buy and sell there
act out the library conversation that begins “I have to return some books.”
ask to check out books and answer “Can I see your library card?”
name library actions: look for a book, talk to the librarian, wait in line, wear headphones
point someone out: “He's the one who's carrying the books.”
read “Library of Celsus” from Turkey and tell key facts about this very old library

units.title: School Link 4 · Metric system of measurement

objectives.text: learn metric units like meters, kilograms and liters and what each one measures
measure different things and write a report about their measurements
compare two measurements and say which thing is longer or heavier
write the names of places with capital letters, like Seoul and Mount Fuji
act out the Grand Canyon conversation that begins “What did you do last summer?”
name experiences: ride in a hot air balloon, see a play, visit the Eiffel Tower
ask and answer “Have you ever been to a library?” and “Has he ever gone camping?”
tell a partner about a trip they took and what they liked best
read “A Hot Spring for Monkeys” from Japan and tell facts about the monkeys
act out the skiing conversation that begins “You're very good at skiing.”
name things young children learn: tie her shoes, use chopsticks, peel a banana, get dressed
ask and answer “What could Ted do when he was four?” using could and couldn't
tell what they could or couldn't do by themselves when they were four
read “How to Use Chopsticks” and explain the steps in order
learn how the Wright Brothers built and flew the first airplane
make and fly a paper helicopter by following the steps
tell how their paper helicopter flew and what made it spin
write names of special things with capital letters, like holidays, days and months
act out the conversation about an old picture book that begins “What's that?”
name things people keep doing: learn French, live in London, teach English, wait for a bus
ask and answer “How long has she been teaching English?” with “for three years”
tell how long they have had something, using since and for
read “The Family from Vietnam” and tell what they learned about the family's life in the USA
act out the conversation about wishes that begins “This is our last summer in elementary school.”
share wishes for the future, like “I wish I could travel the world.”
name big dreams: climb Mount Fuji, invent a flying car, win a gold medal, own a farm
ask and answer “What would she do if she could do anything in the world?”
read “Saving Earth” from Sweden and tell what people can do to help the planet
learn what robots are and how some machines can think and learn
write a report about a special robot or a machine that can think and learn
check their writing for capital letters, end marks and complete sentences
tell the class how their robot or machine helps people
